entities.name: Boutonniere deformity
observations: Central-slip disruption or insufficiency with triangular-ligament attenuation causes volar migration of the lateral bands, PIP flexion, and often secondary DIP hyperextension.
Dorsal repositioning of the lateral bands is a reconstructive maneuver used to correct established or chronic boutonniere deformity.

entities.name: Swan-neck deformity
observations: Swan-neck reconstruction uses volar rather than dorsal translocation of the lateral bands, distinguishing it from the maneuver in this scenario.

entities.name: Mallet finger deformity
observations: Mallet finger reflects terminal extensor tendon failure at the DIP joint and is not the central-slip/lateral-band pathology described here.
